author: Axaxia88
name: A World of Kindness
text:
The Pelican Who Found His Own Way to School 💖

In 1989, something unusual happened in the Japanese city of Ube. Children at a nursery school were playing in the dirt when a pink pelican with a wide wingspan came gliding down into the middle of the playground, as if he had simply arrived for class.

His name was Kattakun. He lived in Tokiwa Park, on an island in the middle of the lake. Not far away was Meiko Nursery School. No one took him to school. No one kept him in a cage and carried him there. Every day, he flew about 800 metres, went into the classroom, stood beside the piano, swayed his neck along with the songs, and then flew back to the island.

That may be the most beautiful part of the story. Kattakun was not turned into a household pet. Nor did he live simply as a bird on the lake. He found a path somewhere in between: spending his mornings at school with the children, then returning home to his flock.

At the nursery school, the children wore uniforms, lined up and sang along with the music. It was their way of greeting one another and saying: we are in the same class. Kattakun did something similar. 

He walked along the glass corridor, entered the room and stood beside the teacher as she played the piano. The children touched his beak and held his wings. Some even sat on his back. He did not become angry or fly away.

To the children, he was not “a strange animal from the zoo”. He was a classmate, different only in having a pouch beneath his bill and the ability to fly.

One day, the school was having its doors and roof repaired. From the sky, Kattakun could no longer recognise the building. He became lost. But when he saw the teacher and the children walking along the road below, he landed and walked alongside them into the classroom. He was not looking for a building. He was looking for people he knew.

Kattakun was born in 1985. He was hatched from an egg by people and hand-reared. Because he grew up around humans, he was not afraid of children, the sound of the piano or the noise of the playground. That was what made it possible for a pelican to become a school visitor.

But there was also a price to this closeness. Pink pelicans normally live in flocks, catch fish and keep their distance from people. Kattakun came to trust humans almost completely. 

In 1989, people across Japan saw the story on the news and smiled. Looking back at it now, adults may feel warmth, but also understand something else: the bird had given up much of the caution that comes naturally to a wild creature.

Kattakun died in 2008, at the age of 23. Tokiwa Park still remembers him. The children who once shared a classroom with him have grown up. When they watch the old footage, they see again their winged friend standing beside the piano.

The story needs no miracle. It only needs a sky wide enough for a bird to choose where he wants to go and a classroom open enough to welcome a friend who is different.
